Hi Sara 

Attached are the artifacts we discussed and a short summary of Redwood-verified performance for the recommended configs. Full benchmark report is linked below.

Key takeaways (short):
- redwood-7b-quant @ 8-bit (RTX A5000 class, Dedicated): ~140 TPS sustained, p50=45ms, p95=290ms (512-token workload, batch sizing optimized for latency).
- llama-2-13b-ft @ 16-bit (better quality, higher cost): ~50 TPS sustained, p50=120ms, p95=420ms (near your p95 SLO; recommend canary testing).

Notes on quantization & quality/regression:
- 8-bit quant (we use a llama-adapted PTQ) reduces latency/TPS dramatically but can introduce subtle hallucination regressions on instruction-heavy prompts; recommend running the prompt_set_v1.jsonl + our eval harness for 48-72 hours and review the quality delta metric (we include an example script in eval_harness_instructions.md).
- We recommend starting with redwood-7b-quant for your latency/throughput needs and keeping a fallback route to llama-2-13b-ft for high-quality inference paths (canary % routing).

Artifacts attached: prompt_set_v1.jsonl, redwood_verified_perf_summary.csv, eval_harness_instructions.md
Benchmarks & perf profiles: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/finplus-eval-2026-03
Drive (prompt sets): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-prompt-sets
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FP-2026-0412

Suggested next steps:
1) Run our eval harness against prompt_set_v1 on a small sample (48h).
2) Share initial quality delta results — we'll help interpret and suggest config tweaks.
3) If TPS/latency look good, set up a Dedicated sizing call (Marissa can lead).

If useful I can set up a 30-min review tomorrow to walk the team through the report and canary plan. What time works for you?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
